phases.name: Safety net
phases.description: Pin today's save wire format with golden legacy saves captured from current main, then add the additive ContainerPath value types with unit tests and the hand-ported upstream TestPaths. No production caller changes.

steps.name: Capture golden legacy saves and restore characterization tests
steps.description: S0. Before any type change, capture saves from current main (mid-tunnel, after a once-only choice, with visit counts, at a choice point) as committed fixtures, plus restore-and-continue characterization tests. Test-only, green from the start.
criteria: Mid-tunnel, once-only-chosen, visit-count and choice-point goldens are captured by unmodified Story.saveState() at commit 54481ef (current main), recorded in the test file header
Each golden save restored into a fresh story yields the same continue output and choices as the uninterrupted playthrough from that point
Saving immediately after restoring each golden yields canonical (sorted-key) JSON bytes identical to the golden's canonical form
All new characterization tests pass on current main with no production code changed
Manual mutation check done: mutating the restore path makes a golden test fail; each mutation and outcome reported in the commit message
steps.scenario_name: S0 golden legacy saves restore and continue
implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM (project convention, CLAUDE.md): Swift Testing, backtick test names (string-label @Test("…") forbidden), example-based and parametrized (@Test(arguments:)) tests; behavioural truth from the inklecate oracle fixtures and the upstream conformance suite. No property-testing library is used in this project; express round-trip/invariant checks as parametrized tests over representative inputs.

This is the D4/ADR-018 safety net. Provenance: the golden files are produced by the unmodified Story.saveState() at commit 54481ef (main HEAD when this roadmap was written; if main has moved, use the then-current HEAD and record that SHA instead) before 01-02 lands, and are never regenerated afterwards. Record the commit SHA, the source fixture and the play route of each golden in the test file header.

Drive the saves from existing inklecate-produced fixtures (e.g. slice-t1-tunnels / slice-t2-nested-tunnels for a non-empty return stack, slice01-once-only for chosen choice targets, slice03-read-counts for visit counts). Hand-crafted story JSON is not allowed (project memory: real compiler JSON only).
Re-save check: compare canonical JSON (decode to Foundation objects, re-serialize with sorted keys) byte-for-byte. This gives both structural and byte identity independent of dictionary ordering.

Each source fixture must have content and a choice after the saved position, so restore-and-continue proves the flow resumes and reaches a later choice point (CLAUDE.md 'A fixture must continue past the construct it pins').

A function-return frame cannot be saved mid-function (no choices inside functions); the 'fnret:path|N' wire form is covered by the 02-06 codec round-trip tests instead. Record this in a comment in the test file.
Fixtures go flat in Tests/SwiftInkRuntimeTests/Fixtures/ (bundled via .process("Fixtures")); prefer one parametrized test over the four golden files.
Green from the start, test-only: no .disabled trait is needed (D8). No production code is committed, so no CodeScene check applies.

MANUAL MUTATION CHECK (test-only variant): to prove the goldens have teeth, temporarily mutate the restore path in production code (e.g. skip decoding one StoryState field such as visitCounts or chosenChoiceTargets, or mis-parse a return-stack entry), run the new tests, confirm a golden test fails, and revert. Report each mutation and its outcome in the commit message; never commit a mutation.
Commit to main through the pre-commit gate (SwiftLint --strict + full swift test); never bypass.

implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM (project convention, CLAUDE.md): Swift Testing, backtick test names (string-label @Test("…") forbidden), example-based and parametrized (@Test(arguments:)) tests; behavioural truth from the inklecate oracle fixtures and the upstream conformance suite. GUARD: full `swift test` green, and the failure messages of `INKSWIFT_CONFORMANCE_BACKLOG=1 swift test --skip-build --filter UpstreamConformance` must be identical before and after the step (capture before, diff after), except that TestPaths leaves the backlog; record the diff in the commit message.

Shape per D1/ADR-016: ContainerPath (absolute, [PathComponent]); PathReference = absolute(ContainerPath) | relative(parentSteps, tail); PathComponent = index(Int) | name(String); synthesised Hashable; equality is structural, not container identity (knot.0 and knot.c-0 stay distinct).

Parse never fails: '' = root, leading '.' = relative, leading carets counted into parentSteps (raw count; caret semantics stay in the resolver, 02-01). inklecate emits carets only leading; a mid-path '^' must still parse without failing and round-trip.

Parse corpus (round-trip `PathReference(parsing: s).description == s` must hold for all): every path string occurring in the committed .ink.json fixtures under Tests/SwiftInkRuntimeTests/Fixtures, including Fixtures/Conformance/ (divert targets, read-count paths, choice targets, tunnel and f() targets, pushed divert targets), plus edge cases "", ".^", ".^.^.x", "a.0.g-2", "0", a digits-only name, and a mid-path "^". Collect the fixture strings in the test by walking the JSON, not by hand-copying.

Hand-port TestPaths (upstream Tests.cs:1526) into scripts/conformance/overrides/TestPaths.swift, adapting C# Path calls to the new types. Remove TestPaths' entry from scripts/conformance/known-failures.json and regenerate with `scripts/conformance/import_upstream_tests.py /Users/maartene/Downloads/ink /Users/maartene/Downloads/inklecate_mac/inklecate`; commit the regenerated UpstreamConformance03Tests.swift, never hand-edit generated files.

steps.name: Type-check tunnel and function pops with C# errors
steps.description: S7. Refuse a pop whose frame kind mismatches, or whose stack is empty: append the exact C# message to currentErrors and end the flow (ADR-017). Errors live in memory only and are cleared by restoreState and moveToKnot (D7). ATs are written inside this step (D8).

Empty-stack pops report exactly 'Found tunnel onwards statement (->->), when expected end of flow (-> END or choice)' or 'Found function return statement (~ return), when expected end of flow (-> END or choice)'

steps.scenario_name: S7 type-checked tunnel and function pops
implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM (project convention, CLAUDE.md): Swift Testing, backtick test names (string-label @Test("…") forbidden), example-based and parametrized (@Test(arguments:)) tests; behavioural truth from the inklecate oracle fixtures and the upstream conformance suite. No property-testing library is used in this project; express round-trip/invariant checks as parametrized tests over representative inputs.

Per D8 there is no DISTILL wave: write the ATs in this step (RED, then GREEN, then COMMIT). The ATs are never committed .disabled; finalize check `grep -rn "\.disabled(" Tests/SwiftInkRuntimeTests/Acceptance` returns nothing.

Exact messages (Story.cs:1275-1288; popped = the requested pop, expected = the current frame's name, or end of flow when the stack cannot pop): (1) 'Found tunnel onwards statement (->->), when expected function return statement (~ return)'; (2) 'Found function return statement (~ return), when expected tunnel onwards statement (->->)'; (3) 'Found tunnel onwards statement (->->), when expected end of flow (-> END or choice)'; (4) 'Found function return statement (~ return), when expected end of flow (-> END or choice)'. Assert currentErrors equals exactly one of these and canContinue == false.

Fixture routes, one fixture per scenario. inklecate rejects `~ return` in a knot not declared as a function (compiler/ParsedHierarchy/FlowBase.cs ~185), and a story stops at its first refusal, so each scenario needs its own story. (a) pop-tunnel-onwards-over-function: a function, called from an expression, plain-diverts into a knot that ends in `->->`. (b) pop-function-return-over-tunnel: a tunnel body (entered with `-> t ->`) plain-diverts `-> f` into a `== function f ==` knot ending in `~ return`. (c) pop-tunnel-onwards-empty-stack: a top-level plain divert into a knot ending in `->->`. (d) pop-function-return-empty-stack: a top-level plain divert into a function knot ending in `~ return`. (e) pop-function-exhaustion-over-tunnel: a tunnel body plain-diverts into a function knot whose body runs out without `~ return`. Per ADR-017 decision 2, implicit exhaustion pops only a function frame, so the tunnel frame must not be consumed. Pin what the reference does there, an error or a plain end of flow.

Verification per fixture: compile each .ink with inklecate (/Users/maartene/Downloads/inklecate_mac/inklecate); never hand-craft JSON. Where the reference produces a runtime error, confirm its text through the InkSwift JS bridge (reference runtime) before pinning it in the AT. If a route is impossible (compile rejection, or the reference does not reach the intended frame state), record why in the test file and pick another route for the same scenario.

Every fixture puts prose, then a choice, after the offending construct in the same scope, and the AT asserts that content does NOT play (CLAUDE.md 'A fixture must continue past the construct it pins'): an engine that silently walks on would show it and fail.

D7: the error list lives in InkEngine memory, not in StoryState, and is never written to a save; restoreState and moveToKnot clear it. currentErrors (currently always []) returns it; the Story facade already delegates, so no public API change. ATs: after a refusal, saveState() then restoreState() yields empty currentErrors, and moveToKnot clears them and the story continues.
The tunnel-return-into-container follow-up remains out of scope. The well-formed case is guarded by the existing tunnel/function oracle fixtures and the conformance harness's hadError check.

Conformance: capture the backlog failure messages (`INKSWIFT_CONFORMANCE_BACKLOG=1 swift test --skip-build --filter UpstreamConformance`) before and after. Messages may change only for tests exercising pops; record each diff in the commit message. Any upstream test that now passes: remove its scripts/conformance/known-failures.json entry and regenerate with scripts/conformance/import_upstream_tests.py so it runs in the main suite.

MANUAL MUTATION CHECK (CLAUDE.md 'Mutation Testing Strategy'): before COMMIT, pick 3-5 plausible-bug mutations in the production code this step changed (flip a condition/comparison, drop a branch or early return, swap cases, return a default instead of the computed value, delete a state update, off-by-one an index/caret count). Apply one at a time, run the step's tests plus the suites guarding that code, record caught/survived, revert. A survivor needs a killing test or a recorded equivalence argument. Report each mutation and its outcome in the commit message; never commit a mutation.

CODE HEALTH: self-check every changed production file with the bundled CodeScene CLI (`$(ls -d ~/Library/Caches/codehealth-mcp/MCP-*/cs | tail -1) review --output-format json <file>`, run from the repo root, needs network) against the main baseline before COMMIT; gate >=9.5 approve, 9–9.5 report what remains, <9 rework. The orchestrator also reviews the step with the CodeScene MCP afterwards.
Commit to main through the pre-commit gate (SwiftLint --strict + full swift test); never bypass.

validation.notes: Approved on re-review (all 12 findings resolved). 02-03 and 02-04 (13 files each) accepted at that size by the orchestrator: a payload type change breaks compilation of every constructor/match site, so each must land in one commit; they are split by concern (S4a/S4b). 03-01 fixture (e): the crafter decides the expected outcome from the C# source and JS bridge BEFORE RED and writes it into criterion 3.
